parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A measurement of an old copper coin or fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: The cubit was an old unit of measure based on the forearm, used in biblical times.

clue.text: These drinks are working at last!

definitions.text: These drinks are working at last!

parts.words: These drinks are working at last!
parts.note: reads as relief that the drinks are taking effect, but describes iced fruit-and-wine drinks and also shoemakers, who work at a last, the foot-shaped block

explanation.surface: A drinker relieved that the alcohol is finally kicking in.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped form a shoe-mender works on; the same word names a sherry-and-fruit drink. In British slang it also means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both menders of shoes and certain iced wine punches share this name, so the clue's drinks and workers coincide.

clue.text: New action to support British gardens of this kind

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the following letters come after the first
new signals that the word action is made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A fresh campaign backing Britain's gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal; 'to support' works because in a down answer the letters below hold up the B above them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kew and similar plant collections are called botanic gardens, so the adjective names gardens of that kind.

indicators.note: returning means the word for the huntsman's gathering is read backwards

parts.note: a meet is the assembly of riders and hounds that a huntsman attends, standing loosely for him

explanation.surface: A hunter coming home carrying an animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a noun, a skin, but here it is the verb: to rain hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pelt down and to pour are both said of heavy rain.

parts.note: could be a scratchy knitted top worn at the seaside, but describes a tiny hopping crustacean or biting insect of the shore

explanation.surface: A scratchy woollen pullover worn on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a British sweater; it is a creature that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: This small shore creature leaps about on beaches and its bite leaves itchy marks.

parts.note: inspiration is literally breathing in, and an air is a tune, so a device that treats breathed air could also be one who arranges tunes

explanation.surface: Something that helps a composer find ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' means drawing in breath, and an 'air' is a melody, so the machine's name doubles as a tune-arranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooling unit makes room atmosphere pleasant to breathe, and taken apart its name suggests someone who prepares melodies.

clue.text: Bird dead, with no tail? You can say that again!

definitions.text: Bird dead, with no tail? You can say that again!

parts.words: Bird dead, with no tail? You can say that again!
parts.note: an extinct flightless bird, dead in the proverbial phrase, whose name is one short syllable repeated

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing emphatically about a tailless dead bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is famously extinct ('dead as a ...'), and its name is a syllable said twice, hence 'You can say that again!'
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct Mauritian bird is the byword for something dead and gone.

parts.note: a lakeside town in Switzerland, which said aloud with packed sounds like the name of the 1925 European treaty signed there

explanation.surface: Word has it a Swiss holiday town is crowded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packed, we hear' sounds like 'pact': the Locarno Pact of 1925 was signed in this resort on Lake Maggiore.
explanation.definitionFit: The town on Lake Maggiore is a well-known resort in Switzerland's Ticino region.

parts.note: all means everybody
O is ring-shaped
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Permitting the whole group to telephone the women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit or sanction something is to give it authority.

clue.text: Something to cheer up suffering patients instead?

definitions.text: Something to cheer up suffering patients instead?

parts.words: Something to cheer up suffering patients instead?
parts.note: medication given to lift the mood of patients who are low, working against their gloom

explanation.surface: A remedy offered to unhappy patients in place of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug's name splits as against a depressant: it works against what pushes the spirits down.
explanation.definitionFit: Such medication is prescribed to relieve clinical depression and lift mood.

clue.text: Bird given drink at end of garden

parts.note: bitter is a British type of beer

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: Someone offered a pint at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a hoppy British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A booming marsh heron is the familiar example of this wading bird.

indicators.note: to admit means the following abbreviation is taken inside the word for spoke

parts.note: a radial is a spoke or line running out from a centre

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician talking in order to let a Tory in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past of 'speak'; it is a wheel's spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone favouring broad progressive reform.

definitions.meaning: to come down and alight, as a bird or aircraft does
a nation or territory, as in a foreign realm

explanation.surface: Moving out to live in rural parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft comes down to settle on the ground; a nation is also called a realm or territory.

clue.text: Athenian doctor in the money, commonly

indicators.note: in places the doctor's abbreviation inside the slang word for money

parts.note: tin is colloquial British slang for money
MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A Greek physician who is very rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon is a citizen of Athens who renounces mankind.

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its central letter G
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A late-night argument that escalates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the mid of 'night', its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow and to develop both mean to increase or mature.

parts.note: S is the clothing size abbreviation for small
mock means imitation, like a dummy

explanation.surface: A shop mannequin in petite size modelling a top.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose overgarment, often gathered, is worn like a loose shirt or tunic.

definitions.meaning: too high, as of a price
to leave in liquid, as with tea

explanation.surface: An over-the-top bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A price can be described as too high in this way, and to steep tea is to infuse it in water.

clue.text: Good word or term no comedian used?

indicators.note: used signals that the letters are taken and reworked into another form

explanation.surface: A compliment, or a phrase no stand-up has ever used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' rearranges TERM NO COMEDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting in a good word for someone is endorsing them, a kind of reference.

clue.text: But this Australian flier should not be plucked

definitions.text: But this Australian flier should not be plucked

parts.words: But this Australian flier should not be plucked
parts.note: plucking a stringed instrument is fine, but a bird should not be plucked, and this Australian bird carries the name of a harp-like instrument

explanation.surface: A conservation plea: leave the feathers on this Aussie bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's tail resembles a small harp, which is played by plucking its strings; birds are plucked of feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian songbird is famous for its harp-shaped tail and mimicry.

parts.note: looks like the latest medical approach, but means therapy using an electric current

explanation.surface: The therapy in fashion today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day'; it is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: This therapy applies electrical stimulation to the body.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tedious stage of an exclusive motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal mind is prosaic and unimaginative, so the word can mean matter-of-fact and dull.

clue.text: Con brings a profit on street

parts.note: gain means profit

explanation.surface: A swindle that pays off on the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle; it is the 'con' of pros and cons, opposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros and cons are points for and opposed, so con means opposed to.

definitions.meaning: tennis is played in these units of games
puts down or places, as a car is placed

explanation.surface: Tennis courts in public gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis match is made up of these scoring units, and to park something is to put it down.

indicators.note: embroidered suggests something worked over and embellished, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Dull clothing that has been decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted colours are called subdued or plain, the sense of drab.

clue.text: Racecourse tax after the first of August

indicators.note: after places the tax word behind the first letter
the first of takes the opening letter of the month named

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A levy coming due after early August.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT survives in 'scot-free', untaxed. ASCOT is the royal racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a famous horse-racing venue.

definitions.meaning: Latin for watch out, used as a warning by British public schoolboys

explanation.surface: A warning about boys hiding in a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolboy slang borrowed the Latin warning to keep watch, and a hollow in rock is the other sense.

clue.text: Sunday, day in Germany set aside for men

parts.note: Tag is German for day

explanation.surface: A German Sunday reserved for the men only.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party or stag night is a men-only event.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag do is a male-only party, so the word describes things for men only.

indicators.note: announced means the word for tender is spoken aloud and written as it sounds

parts.note: to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A dam engineer's bid read out.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa, an 8th-century king of Mercia, built Offa's Dyke along the English-Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa of Mercia ordered the great earthwork named after him.

parts.note: a solemn curse in surface form, but describes the square cap worn on a priest's head

explanation.surface: Blame laid on Dad: let the consequences fall on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' is a Catholic priest, who may wear this square cap.
explanation.definitionFit: This stiff square hat is worn by Roman Catholic clergy.

indicators.note: announced means the three letters are read aloud as their names

parts.note: the letters F, N, D said by name

explanation.surface: An abbreviation read out as a title of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a Turkish title of respect for a learned or educated man.

clue.text: Greta Lee thrown out, put in lower class

indicators.note: thrown out suggests being cast away, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress named Greta Lee ejected and demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs or players are relegated when moved down a division.

explanation.surface: Was an actor responsible for performing?
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a deed and performing a part on stage share the same past-tense verb.
